findings.title: Toxic flow within 'comfyui-mcp': executes commands + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 83 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and can reach the network, which is remote code execution with a delivery channel rather than a hint of one. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): agentistics_session_away
findings.detail: The description of 'agentistics__mcp.agentistics_session_away' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: concealment. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: concealment, entropy, log_len, imperative_density.

evidence.description: Read or switch AUTONOMOUS MODE, or send the owner a notice while autonomous — the fleet works on its own, without asking permission or questions (the owner may be asleep or travelling). While it is on, every new session is born in the no-questions approval mode unless its caller names a mode. With no `on` it reports the state (`active`, `until`, what is pre-authorised). With `on: true` it switches it on: `until` is an ISO instant (omit = until the owner says they are back), `authorised` lists wh

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

- analyze: Onsets, BPM, confidence and duration. Params: source (asset id, data URL or URL),
  sensitivity, minGap. Read-only — run it first to see what the track gives you.
- animate_to_beat: Write a keyframe track that pulses on the beat. Params: itemId, plus EITHER

  detected tempo instead of the raw onsets — the difference

evidence.description: Checks that the Reclaim attestor works from this machine by proving a public CoinGecko price request with a throwaway key. It uses no credential, provider, or logged-in site, and takes up to 45 seconds (about 8 when healthy). findings.title: Toxic flow within 'devharness': executes commands + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 2 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and can reach the network, which is remote code execution with a delivery channel rather than a hint of one. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'crawlora-mcp': executes commands + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 588 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and can reach the network, which is remote code execution with a delivery channel rather than a hint of one. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'quackai__q402-mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 61 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send data to an address it controls. A single prompt is enough to turn 'summarise this config' into a credential leak. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'onesi__genesis-mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 304 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send data to an address it controls. A single prompt is enough to turn 'summarise this config' into a credential leak. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): get_project_info
findings.detail: The description of 'audionaut-mcp.get_project_info' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: injection_markers. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: injection_markers, entropy, imperative_density.

evidence.description: Summarizes an Audionaut project: tempo, tracks, clips with positions/durations and their audio files. Set raw=true for the full persistence JSON instead of the summary.

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

evidence.description:
Turn a list of skillIds into what they ACTUALLY produce: the concrete tools they add and the text they append to the system prompt. Nothing is created or changed.
This is how you check the skill system is working. Two failures only show up here: a skillId that resolves to nothing (typo, or a skill the account cannot see — the assistant just silently lacks the capability), and skills whose prompt additions contradict each other.
Read it together with try_assistant: this says what the assistant wa

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'cognitiondesk__mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 47 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send data to an address it controls. A single prompt is enough to turn 'summarise this config' into a credential leak. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'cognitiondesk__mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends email or messages
findings.detail: 126 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends email or messages. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send mail. This is the postmark-mcp shape: the mail tool was legitimate, the credentials were reachable, and the combination was the incident. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'cognitiondesk__mcp': executes commands + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 6 combination(s) exist where one tool executes commands and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they executes commands and can reach the network, which is remote code execution with a delivery channel rather than a hint of one. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): read_filament_docs
findings.detail: The description of 'filament-mcp.read_filament_docs' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: injection_markers. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: injection_markers, entropy, imperative_density.

evidence.description: Reads one Filament documentation page. Use `section` to extract a single heading instead of the whole page — most pages are far larger than the part you need. Find paths with list_filament_docs or search_filament_docs. Examples: "resources/overview", "forms/select", "tables/columns/text".

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): execute_command
findings.detail: The description of 'iflow-mcp__super-win-cli-mcp-server.execute_command' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: markup_injection. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: markup_injection, entropy, log_len, imperative_density.

evidence.description:
Execute a command in the specified shell (powershell, cmd, or gitbash)

Example usage (PowerShell):
```json
{
  "shell": "powershell",
  "command": "Get-Process | Select-Object -First 5",
  "workingDir": "C:\Users\username"
}
```

Example usage (CMD):
```json
{
  "shell": "cmd",
  "command": "dir /b",
  "workingDir": "C:\Projects"
}
```

Example usage (Git Bash):
```json
{
  "shell": "gitbash",
  "command": "ls -la",
  "workingDir": "/c/Users/username"
}
```

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.
